title: The Notebook That Included Wrong Answers
fact_notes: 人物・町・行事・数値や結果は架空の事例。実在の統計や研究結果ではない。参考リンクは制作台帳であり、実証資料ではない。

sentences.en: A student named Yuto usually copied only correct solutions into his mathematics notebook after receiving feedback on a classroom exercise.
sentences.ja: ユウトという生徒は授業の練習問題でフィードバックを受けた後、たいてい正しい解答だけを数学のノートに写した。

sentences.en: He believed that replacing his mistakes with accurate solutions would make the notebook more useful when he prepared for an examination.
sentences.ja: 誤りを正しい解答に置き換えると試験準備でノートがより役立つと考えた。

sentences.en: By the end of each week, the pages looked neat and contained a clear record of the procedures that the teacher had demonstrated.
sentences.ja: 毎週末にはページは整然とし、教師が実演した手順が明確に記録されていた。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, Yuto sometimes repeated an earlier mistake because he could not remember why his original approach had seemed reasonable.
sentences.ja: それでも元の方法がなぜ妥当に思えたか思い出せず、以前の誤りを繰り返すことがあった。

sentences.en: His teacher suggested that a useful learning record might preserve a student's initial reasoning instead of presenting only successful outcomes.
sentences.ja: 教師は有用な学習記録には成功した結果だけでなく生徒の最初の推論も残す方法があると提案した。

sentences.en: She asked him to divide a new notebook page into three sections labeled original idea, evidence of a problem, and revised approach.
sentences.ja: 新しいページを「最初の考え」「問題を示す根拠」「修正した方法」の三区画に分けるよう求めた。

sentences.en: The first section would contain what Yuto had actually thought before finding out whether his answer was correct.
sentences.ja: 第一の区画には正誤が分かる前にユウトが実際に考えたことを書く。

sentences.en: In the second section, he would explain which feature of the problem or which calculation showed that his approach needed reconsideration.
sentences.ja: 第二の区画では問題のどの特徴や計算が考え直す必要性を示したか説明する。

sentences.en: At first, Yuto found the additional writing inconvenient because it took more time than simply copying the teacher's correct solution.
sentences.ja: 最初ユウトは正解を写すだけより時間がかかるので追加の記述を面倒に感じた。

sentences.en: However, the new format helped him discover that several apparently unrelated mistakes arose from a similar misunderstanding of the question.
sentences.ja: しかし新しい形式により、一見無関係な複数の誤りが問題への似た誤解から生じていると分かった。

sentences.en: He sometimes treated information about a whole group as though it described every individual member of that group.
sentences.ja: 彼はときに集団全体の情報を、その集団の個々の構成員すべてについての情報であるかのように扱った。

sentences.en: After identifying that pattern, he began asking himself whether a statement referred to an individual or an entire group before attempting a calculation.
sentences.ja: その傾向を把握した後、計算前に記述が個人と集団全体のどちらを指すか自問するようになった。

sentences.en: Yuto did not use the detailed record for every incorrect answer because some mistakes involved nothing more than an accidental copying error.
sentences.ja: 誤答のすべてに詳細記録を使ったわけではない。単なる偶発的な転記ミスに過ぎないものもあったからだ。

sentences.en: Instead, he selected mistakes that revealed a misunderstanding or suggested that he had used an unsuitable strategy for an unfamiliar problem.
sentences.ja: 代わりに、誤解や不慣れな問題に不適切な方略を使ったことを示す誤りを選んだ。

sentences.en: Before the next practice examination, he reviewed these records and attempted similar questions without first looking at his revised solutions.
sentences.ja: 次の模試前、記録を見直し、修正後の解答を先に見ず類題に挑戦した。

sentences.en: The teacher encouraged him to use his subsequent performance as one indication of whether the notebook was actually helping him learn.
sentences.ja: 教師はその後の出来を、ノートが実際に学習を助けているかの一つの指標として使うよう促した。

sentences.en: The project did not provide proof that keeping a particular kind of notebook would improve the performance of every mathematics student.
sentences.ja: 活動は特定のノートがすべての数学学習者の成績を向上させるという証明にはならなかった。

sentences.en: It did, however, help Yuto understand that correcting a written answer and correcting the reasoning behind that answer were different activities.
sentences.ja: しかしユウトが答案の修正とその背後の推論の修正が異なる活動だと理解する助けになった。

sentences.en: A mistake can become useful evidence when a learner examines the conditions under which an apparently sensible decision produced an incorrect result.
sentences.ja: 一見妥当な判断が誤った結果をもたらした条件を検討するとき、誤りは有用な証拠となり得る。

sentences.en: For Yuto, a notebook became more than a collection of correct answers; it became a record of how his understanding had changed.
sentences.ja: ユウトにとってノートは正解集以上のものとなり、理解がどう変わったかを記録するものになった。

questions.prompt: What did Yuto usually write after feedback?
options: Only the teacher's comments.
Every answer from other students.
A list of future lesson dates.
Only correct solutions.

questions.prompt: Why did he sometimes repeat earlier mistakes?
options: He had never received correct solutions.
He had not preserved the reasoning that led to them.
He was required to use the same wrong answer.
He had lost every notebook page.
questions.explanation_ja: 元の考えがなぜ妥当と思えたか残っていなかった。

questions.prompt: What did the teacher ask him to preserve?
options: Only the final answers for the entire class.
The dates of all mathematics examinations.
His initial idea and evidence of the problem as well as the revised approach.
A list of mistakes without corrections.
questions.explanation_ja: 最初の考え、問題の根拠、修正方法を記録。

questions.prompt: What was the purpose of the second section?
options: Explain what showed a need to reconsider the approach.
Copy an unrelated textbook paragraph.
Record only the examination score.
Remove the original reasoning from the page.
questions.explanation_ja: どの情報・計算が再考を促したか記す。

questions.prompt: What did Yuto discover about some different mistakes?
options: They had all been caused by a broken calculator.
They shared a similar misunderstanding.
They were all accidental copying errors.
They resulted from contradictory teacher instructions.
questions.explanation_ja: 似た誤解から生じていた。

questions.prompt: What did he begin checking before calculations?
options: Whether the page was perfectly tidy.
Whether the teacher had written the answer already.
Whether his notebook had enough blank pages.
Whether a statement referred to an individual or a whole group.
questions.explanation_ja: 対象が個人か集団かを確認。

questions.prompt: Which mistakes did he select for detailed records?
options: Mistakes showing a misunderstanding or unsuitable strategy.
Every accidental spelling mistake.
All correctly solved exercises.
Only answers with large numbers.
questions.explanation_ja: 考え方の誤りが表れたもの。

questions.prompt: Why did he try similar questions without viewing the revised answers?
options: To prevent the teacher from checking his notebook.
To make the new questions deliberately harder.
To test whether he could use the corrected reasoning independently.
To avoid learning the correct solutions.
questions.explanation_ja: 修正した理解を自力で活用できるか確かめる。

questions.prompt: What does reasoning mean in context?
options: The final number alone.
A list of textbook chapters.
An official examination date.
The process of thinking toward a conclusion.
A neat notebook guarantees success for every student.
Examining why a mistake occurred can support deeper correction of understanding.
All incorrect answers must receive exactly the same amount of analysis.
A final correct answer makes previous reasoning unimportant.
questions.explanation_ja: 誤答の原因を分析し理解を修正する。

paraphrases.source: He believed that replacing his mistakes with accurate solutions would make the notebook more useful when he prepared for an examination.
paraphrases.rewrite: He thought that writing correct answers in place of mistakes would improve the notebook as an examination aid.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 正解だけで試験準備に役立つと思った。

paraphrases.source: His teacher suggested that a useful learning record might preserve a student's initial reasoning instead of presenting only successful outcomes.
paraphrases.rewrite: His teacher suggested keeping evidence of how a student first thought, not just the results that were correct.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 初期の考えも残すよう促した。

paraphrases.source: He sometimes treated information about a whole group as though it described every individual member of that group.
paraphrases.rewrite: He sometimes interpreted information about an entire group as information about each person in it.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 集団全体の情報を個人ごとの情報と誤解した。

paraphrases.source: The project did not provide proof that keeping a particular kind of notebook would improve the performance of every mathematics student.
paraphrases.rewrite: The project did not establish that every mathematics student would benefit from this notebook format.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 全生徒への一般化を証明したわけではない。
